newsitem.title: UK: Union urges joint attack on pensions' misselling.
newsitem.headline: Union urges joint attack on pensions' misselling.

text.p: Britain's biggest trade union, UNISON, says it is urging other unions to join it in a united attack against companies guilty of misselling pensions to members and the public.

The union wants to speed up the settlement of claims arising from the misselling scandal in the late 1980s and early 1990s by setting up a joint negotiating strategy and so increase the pressure on the already beleaguered pension companies.
"Members have had enough of delays and grossly inadequate offers from pensions companies," said UNISON assistant general secretary Roger Poole.
"We are determined to protect our members from further financial disadvantage and if that means taking companies to court so be it."
More than one and a half a million people may have been wrongly advised to take out personal pensions instead of staying with occupational schemes between 1988 and 1994.
Companies have come under increasing pressure from the government and regulators to speed up compensation payments to those who lost out.
The government has even instigated a policy of "naming and shaming" firms suspected of dragging their feet.
In 1994 the Securities & Investments Board initiated a widespread review of all personal pensions sold since April 1988.

Since then, firms involved have been set a deadline of the end of 1998 to compensate victims losing out. The final compensation bill for the industry is likely to be well above four billion pounds ($6.4 billion).
Companies who wrongly advised customers to leave occupational pension schemes in the late 1980s and early 1990s have offered to match the benefits of the schemes left.
Last week the company with the greatest number of cases to settle Prudential Corp said it was almost doubling provisions to clear up cases to 450 million pounds.

By joining forces with other trade unions UNISON hopes to settle claims "Instead of looking forward to a happy and comfortable retirement many people are now faced with the nightmare of being forced to scrimp and save just to make ends meet," said Poole.
"This is intolerable and with the combined weight of the union movement we can take on the pensions giant face to face."
-- Simon Cowell, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7721 ($ = 0.628 British Pounds)
